family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at the host branch: look for a persistent green branching mistletoe clump growing directly from woody host tissue. Then inspect the swollen attachment, opposite leathery leaves, tiny reduced flowers and berry-like one-seeded fruits.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Aerial hemiparasitic shrubs on woody hosts; green photosynthetic shoots remain exposed. Local Phoradendron has opposite simple leaves and jointed branching, with haustorial attachment to host tissue.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers are tiny, greenish and reduced, borne in short spikes; local plants may be male or female.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Berry-like one-seeded fruit with sticky viscin that helps the seed adhere to branches.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: The family doorway is the exposed green shrub growing from a woody host branch, not flower color.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: host context → attachment → opposite leaves → flower spike → sticky fruit

steps.title: 1 · See host and mistletoe together
steps.photo_role: whole host branch with mistletoe clump
steps.look_for: A distinct green branching clump growing from another woody plant.

steps.title: 2 · Trace the attachment
steps.look_for: Mistletoe stem entering a swollen host branch.
steps.why_it_matters: This junction is a high-value structural character.

steps.title: 3 · Read the nodes
steps.look_for: Opposite leathery simple leaves on exposed green shoots.

steps.title: 4 · Follow flowers into fruit
steps.look_for: Tiny reduced flowers in short spikes; female shoots later bear berry-like fruits with one sticky seed.

comparisons.title: Santalaceae vs Apodanthaceae
comparisons.rule: Phoradendron exposes a persistent green leafy shoot outside the host; Pilostyles keeps nearly all vegetative tissue inside the host and mainly exposes flowers/fruits through bark.

comparisons.title: Mistletoe vs epiphyte
comparisons.rule: Mistletoe has a structural attachment into host tissue; an ordinary epiphyte simply grows on the surface.

comparisons.title: Mistletoe vs woody vine
comparisons.rule: A vine climbs from its own rooting point; mistletoe grows from a seed established directly on a host branch.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not separate Phoradendron species from berry color or host alone; species routing needs leaf/twig pubescence, inflorescence and current taxonomy.

genera.fast_cue: green aerial mistletoe; opposite leaves; reduced flower spikes; sticky one-seeded fruit

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label host branch, mistletoe stem and attachment zone
outline mistletoe separately from host foliage
show one seed and sticky viscin
label opposite leaves and jointed stem
exposed leafy shoot vs hidden vegetative body
